newsitem.title: USA: U.S High Court to decide state voter registration.
newsitem.headline: U.S High Court to decide state voter registration.

text.p: The Supreme Court said Tuesday it would hear a Justice Department appeal involving Mississippi's practice of applying a 1993 voter registration law just to federal, and not state or local, elections.
The federal law requires states to make voter registration easier and to remove opportunities for discrimination in the registration process.

It requires that states treat every driver's license application as a request for voter registration, accept voter registration applications by mail and distribute applications at various state agencies.
The Justice Department said Mississippi has been the only state to refuse to apply the law's registration procedures to state and local elections.
The Justice Department argued that Mississippi's decision constituted a voting change subject to the voting rights law and must be approved by the attorney general or a federal court.

But a three-judge federal court in Mississippi disagreed, ruling in July that only the state legislature under Mississippi law could decide whether to apply the registration procedures to state and local elections.
The Justice Department appealed the ruling, and the Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in the case early next year, with a decision expected by July.
